newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Steady growth seen in March UK sales.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Steady growth seen in March UK sales.

text.p: British retail sales data for March, due on Wednesday, are expected to show steady growth in high street spending and to paint a more buoyant picture of activity than recent surveys have done.

The figures will be the last before the May 1 election and the next monetary meeting, scheduled for May 7, at which some economists expect an increase in official interest rates from the present 6.0 percent.
"Assuming a Labour victory, they could have a significant bearing on the new chancellor's stance on interest rates," said Philip Shaw, chief economist at Union Plc.

The Reuters consensus forecast is for retail sales to grow a seasonally adjusted 0.3 percent in March after a 0.5 percent rise in February, giving a year-on-year rise of 4.3 percent against 4.4 percent.

Economists say the figures are difficult to forecast at the moment because the leading surveys -- the CBI Distributive Trades Survey and the British Retail Consortium (BRC) Retail Sales Monitor -- have been at odds with the official data.

Dharshini David, an economist at HSBC Markets, notes that the CBI survey implied annual growth in sales of about three percent in January and February while the official figures showed growth of 4.8 percent and 4.4 percent respectively.
She believes the official data are more comprehensive than the more pessimistic CBI and BRC surveys.

Despite the sturdy 0.5 percent month-on-month rise in February retail sales, David said: "There were few signs that the pace of spending on the high street is becoming reckless, with the three-month on three-month rate falling to an 11-month low of 0.7 percent."
"While sales are buoyant, consumers still appear to be price conscious."
She sees March retail sales growth of 0.3 percent month-on-month and 4.3 percent year-on-year, but adds:
"There is a degree of uncertainty surrounding our forecast and we would not be entirely surprised if the official retail sales figures were slightly weaker than expected."

Shaw of Union Plc says both the CBI and BRC surveys for March are consistent with a modest increase in sales volumes during the month. "Warm weather should also have encouraged consumer activity," he says.
His forecast is for growth of 0.2 percent in the month and 4.2 percent year-on-year.

"Although this would represent just a small rise on the month, it is consistent with a continued strengthening in high street spending and would encourage rather than discourage a post-election base rate increase," Shaw says.

David Smith, an economist at Williams de Broe, says Easter is likely to have boosted the seasonally adjusted figures in March. "We are forecasting that the volume of retail sales expanded by 0.5 percent to give a yearly rise of 4.6 percent."
